newsitem.title: USA: Dell introduces new low-priced pentium servers.
newsitem.headline: Dell introduces new low-priced pentium servers.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp. introduced on Monday a new line of network server computers based on the advanced Pentium Pro chip, at prices Dell Chief Executive Michael Dell said will result in an "assault" on the server market.

The first product in the new line, the PowerEdge 2100, priced at $3,799, is a 200 megahertz, single-processor entry-level server. Servers are computers that link PCs into small networks and connect other servers to form larger networks.
According to Dell, the 2100 will sell for as much as 45 percent below the price of many single processor Pentium-based network servers and will be available this month.
In a few months, Dell plans to introduce the more powerful PowerEdge 4100, and then the PowerEdge 6100, for the high end of the market.
Dell said the company will use the same direct mail distribution and pricing strategies it uses in the desktop market, to gain share in the server market.

Dell said he expected profit margins in the server industry "to come significantly under pressure because of Dell's initiative," on lower prices, stating that most computer makers subsidise their personal computer and notebook prices by charging high server prices.
The leading server makers are Compaq Computer Corp., Hewlett-Packard Co. and International Business Machines Corp.
"We do not rely on server profit nor do we intend to rely on our server business to subsidise our notebook and desktops," Dell said.
He said the company may see its margins improve if it is able to catch a larger share of the server market.
Dell stock was off $1.125 at $67.875 on the Nasdaq system in afternoon trading.
